release.name: containerd 2.4.1
release.body:
Welcome to the v2.4.1 release of containerd! The first patch release for containerd 2.4 contains various fixes and updates including a security patch. ### Security Updates * **containerd** * [**CVE-2026-53493**](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-pg57-6jwg-q645) ### Highlights #### Container Runtime Interface (CRI) * Fix bug where failed container start cleanup leaked tasks and prevented container removal ([#14223](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14223)) * Fix bug where container creation failed when SELinux relabeling was unsupported by the filesystem ([#14212](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14212)) #### Image Distribution * Fix content upload failures when retrying fetch content after reaching EOF ([#14197](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14197)) #### Snapshotters * Apply hardening to filter ID-mapping labels from image annotations during unpack ([#14200](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14200)) #### ctr development tool * Fix bug where arguments following "-" were dropped in "ctr images export" ([#14219](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14219)) * Fix bug where container command arguments were parsed as flags in "ctr run", "ctr containers create", "ctr tasks exec", and "containerd oci-hook" ([#14215](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14215)) * Fix bug where comma-separated flag values were incorrectly split in ctr subcommands ([#14188](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/14188)) Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues. ### Contributors * Samuel Karp * Aysha Afrah Ziya * Chris Henzie * CrazyMax * Maksym Pavlenko * Nan Liu * Sebastiaan van Stijn ### Changes

Dynamically linked with glibc 2.35 (Ubuntu 22.04). * `containerd-static---.tar.gz`: Statically linked. Expected to be used on Linux distributions that do not use glibc >= 2.35. Not position-independent. In addition to containerd, typically you will have to install [runc](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/releases) and [CNI plugins](https://github.com/containernetworking/plugins/releases) from their official sites too. See also the [Getting Started](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md) documentation.

14188.title: [release/2.4] ctr: disable slice flag separator on commands
14188.body:
This is an automated cherry-pick of #14185

```release-note
Fix bug where comma-separated flag values were incorrectly split in ctr subcommands
```
14188.author: k8s-infra-cherrypick-robot

14185.title: ctr: disable slice flag separator on commands
14185.body:
In urfave/cli/v3, child commands do not inherit
DisableSliceFlagSeparator from the root command, unlike in urfave/cli/v2. When containerd migrated to v3 in commit f72829f36, subcommands inadvertently reverted to splitting slice flags on commas, breaking flags that expect comma-separated values such as --mount type=bind,src=/tmp,dst=/host,options=rbind:ro.

Explicitly set DisableSliceFlagSeparator on all cli.Command structs in cmd/ctr/commands, restoring the behavior where slice flags are not split on commas.

Fixes #14181

Assisted-by: Antigravity
14185.author: samuelkarp

14197.title: [release/2.4] remotes: revert closing fetch readers at EOF
14197.body:
This is an automated cherry-pick of #14194

/assign thaJeztah

```release-note
Fix content upload failures when retrying fetch content after reaching EOF
```
14197.author: k8s-infra-cherrypick-robot

14194.title: remotes: revert closing fetch readers at EOF
14194.body:
Revert #13438 to restore registry-cache upload retries, addressing the regression blocking BuildKit containerd v2.4.0 upgrade in https://github.com/moby/buildkit/pull/7173#discussion_r4047433110. Closing the source reader at EOF prevents `content.Copy` from rewinding it when the destination writer requests a retry, causing uploads to fail with `seek on closed reader`.

The HTTP reader already closes its response body at EOF while remaining seekable, preserving CRI progress accounting before a slow commit without the generic wrapper. A separate commit adds regression tests for replaying uploads after HTTP 408, seeking after EOF, and closing the HTTP body exactly once before commit.
14194.author: crazy-max

7173.title: test: Add ability to switch between  cgroupv1 or cgroupv2 for node e2e
7173.body:
For k8s e2e node tests, we want to be able to test both cgroupv1 and
cgroupv2 variants. Currently, the latest version of COS (M97) is running
as cgroupv2 and we would like the add the ability to switch to cgroupv1
for running tests on cgroupv1.

To do this, add a new flag, "CGROUP_MODE" which can be set as v1 or v2.
If the current cgroup configuration does not match the desired config,
the cgroup config will be set via `cgroup_helper` COS utility, and the
node will be rebooted.

Signed-off-by: David Porter <porterdavid@google.com>
7173.author: bobbypage

13438.title: remotes: close fetch reader immediately on EOF
13438.body:
The CRI progress reporter cancels an image pull if it sees no progress
for 5 seconds. It tracks this through active HTTP requests. During
remote fetches, the HTTP response reader is closed via a deferred
call after `content.Copy` completes.

Diagnosis:
`content.Copy` handles both downloading the stream and committing
the writer to the content store. Any delays during the database
commit phase (e.g. from database locks, slow disk syncs, or concurrent
pull deduplication blocks) keep the HTTP connection open. The progress
reporter sees the request is still active (`activeReqs = 1`) but no new
bytes are coming in, leading to a premature timeout cancellation.

Reproduction:
We reproduced this flakiness deterministically on a GCE VM under a
simulated 2 Mbps ingress bandwidth limit using Linux traffic control
ingress policing (`tc filter ... action police rate 2mbit`). Under this
slowness, the download took longer than the progress timeout during the
slow commit phase, triggering context cancellation and failing the
`TestCRIImagePullTimeout/HoldingContentOpenWriterWithLocalPull` test.

Solution:
To fix this, we wrap the HTTP reader in a `closeOnEOFReader` or
`closeOnEOFReadSeeker` before handing it to `content.Copy`. If the
underlying connection reader implements `io.Seeker`, it is dynamically
wrapped in `closeOnEOFReadSeeker` to forward `Seek` operations. This
ensures that O(1) Range seeks are fully preserved during network
resumes or retries. The wrappers automatically close the underlying
network stream as soon as `Read()` returns `io.EOF` (when the download
completes, before the database commit begins). This drops `activeReqs`
to `0` early, freeing the socket and preventing progress timeouts
during commits. A `sync.Once` ensures that subsequent deferred
`Close()` calls do not double-decrement the reporter.

How it was tested:
Verified the fix on a GCE VM under a simulated 2 Mbps ingress
bandwidth limit. Verified seeker safety via standalone logic audits
and trace proofs.

Assisted-by: Antigravity
13438.author: samuelkarp

14200.title: [release/2.4] core/unpack: don't honor id-mapping labels from image annotations
14200.body:

```release-note

```
14200.author: k8s-infra-cherrypick-robot

13855.title: core/unpack: don't honor id-mapping labels from image annotations
13855.body: The unpacker turns each image layer descriptor's annotations into snapshot labels and hands them to the snapshotter's Prepare, and FilterInheritedLabels keeps every containerd.io/snapshot/ key, so it also keeps containerd.io/snapshot/uidmapping and .../gidmapping. The overlay and erofs snapshotters act on those in Prepare by chowning the extracted layer's fs directory to the mapped host uid/gid, and that branch runs whenever the label is present, independent of the snapshotter's remapIDs setting. Layer annotations come straight from the image manifest, so a crafted image can put the mapping labels on a layer and make containerd chown the committed layer directory to an arbitrary host uid/gid during an ordinary pull, with no user-namespace setup involved. Because the committed directory is a shared, reused rootfs lowerdir, that ownership sticks and follows every container built on the layer. I ran into it while tracing where these labels are produced: the id maps are meant to reach the snapshotter from the runtime via WithRemapperLabels at container-prepare time, not from image content. The fix drops only the two id-mapping labels in the unpacker, so the annotation inheritance that remote snapshotters depend on stays intact while image content can no longer reach that chown.
13855.author: aysha-afrah26


14207.title: cri: tolerate wrapped ENOTSUP during relabel
14207.body:
`label.Relabel` can return an `*os.PathError` wrapping `syscall.ENOTSUP` when the source filesystem does not support SELinux extended attributes. The existing direct comparison only recognizes an unwrapped errno, so CRI container creation fails instead of tolerating the unsupported relabel operation.

Tested with:

- `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto go test ./internal/cri/opts`
- `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto make check`
14207.author: liunan-ms

14217.title: ctr: preserve args after "-" in images export
14217.body:
urfave/cli/v3 breaks out of its flag parsing loop when it encounters a "-" positional argument without appending the remaining arguments, causing "ctr images export - <image>" to drop all image references and flags following "-".

When <out> is "-", recover the un-truncated arguments from the parent "images" command lineage and re-parse the tail starting at "-" with a sentinel placeholder so trailing image references and flags are preserved.

This workaround can be removed after the bug is fixed upstream:

* https://github.com/urfave/cli/issues/2418
* https://github.com/urfave/cli/pull/2419

Assisted-by: Antigravity
14217.author: samuelkarp

14223.title: [release/2.4] cri: don't leak task when StartContainer cleanup fails to delete task
14223.body:
This is an automated cherry-pick of #14218

/kind resource-leak

```release-note

```
14223.author: k8s-infra-cherrypick-robot

14218.title: cri: don't leak task when StartContainer cleanup fails to delete task
14218.body:
When `StartContainer` fails after the task is created and the cleanup task delete fails (e.g. it timed out on a stuck shim), the container was recorded as `EXITED` while its task could potentially remained. 

`RemoveContainer` only reaps tasks for `RUNNING` and `UNKNOWN` containers, so every kubelet GC retry failed with "cannot delete running task" and the container was never collected.

Record the container as `UNKNOWN` when task cleanup cannot be confirmed so `RemoveContainer` force-stops it and retries the cleanup.
14218.author: mxpv

14181.title: `ctr`: Subcommands split slice flags (e.g. `--mount`) on commas after migration to `urfave/cli/v3`
14181.body:
### Background:
#### Description
In containerd 2.4.0, `cmd/ctr` was migrated to `urfave/cli/v3`. While `DisableSliceFlagSeparator: true` is set on the root `ctr` command (`cmd/ctr/app/main.go`), child subcommands (`containers create`, `run`, etc.) do **not** inherit this flag in `urfave/cli/v3`.

As a result, slice flags containing commas (such as `--mount type=bind,src=/path,dst=/path,options=rbind:ro`) are erroneously split on commas into separate slice elements with empty destinations, causing container task initialization to fail during `runc` mount setup:

```text
ctr: failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed:
unable to start container process: error during container init:
error mounting "" to rootfs at "": create mountpoint for mount:
mountpoint "/run/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/default/test/rootfs" is on the top of rootfs "/run/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/default/test/rootfs"
```

This regression impacts node workflows, diagnostics, autotests, and GKE Installables.

#### Steps to Reproduce
Run any `ctr` command passing a `--mount` flag with comma-separated options:
```bash
ctr containers create \
  --mount type=bind,src=/var/lib/containerd/binary,dst=/binary,options=bind \
  <image> test
ctr task start -d test
```

Inspecting the container spec (`ctr containers info test`) shows the single `--mount` flag was split into 4 separate mounts:
```json
"mounts": [
    {"destination": "", "type": "bind"},
    {"destination": "", "source": "/var/lib/containerd/binary"},
    {"destination": "/binary"},
    {"destination": "", "options": ["bind"]}
]
```

#### Root Cause
In `urfave/cli/v3` (`flag_slice_base.go` and `command.go`):
- Multi-value slice flags split on commas by default unless `cmd.DisableSliceFlagSeparator == true`.
- When subcommands execute, `setMultiValueParsingConfig` checks `cmd.DisableSliceFlagSeparator` on the active subcommand `cmd`.
- Unlike `useShortOptionHandling()`, `urfave/cli/v3` does not traverse `cmd.Lineage()` for `DisableSliceFlagSeparator` (see also [urfave/cli#1856](https://github.com/urfave/cli/issues/1856)).
- Because `ctr` only sets `DisableSliceFlagSeparator: true` on the root command, all subcommands execute with `DisableSliceFlagSeparator: false`.

#### Proposed Fix
Explicitly set `DisableSliceFlagSeparator: true` on all subcommands where slice flags are accepted, or traverse command definitions when constructing `ctr` commands.
14181.author: chenglongtang1

14208.title: [Regression 2.4.0] ctr run treats container command flags as ctr flags ("flag provided but not defined")
14208.body:
### Description

In containerd 2.4.0, passing container command arguments that begin with a dash (such as `bash -uexc "..."` or `sh -c "..."`) causes `ctr run` to fail with `flag provided but not defined`.

In all previous versions of containerd (containerd 1.7.x and 2.0.x through 2.3.x), `ctr run [flags] Image|RootFS ID [COMMAND] [ARG...]` treated all arguments following `<ID>` as the container process command and arguments. In 2.4.0, `ctr` scans for its own flags across and after positional arguments.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run any container where the command to execute inside the container includes flags:

```bash
ctr run --rm docker.io/library/busybox:latest test-container sh -uexc "echo hello"
```

### Expected Behavior (containerd <= 2.3.x)

The arguments `sh`, `-uexc`, and `"echo hello"` are passed to the container runtime via `oci.WithProcessArgs`. The container executes the command and exits cleanly:

```
+ echo hello
hello
```

### Actual Behavior (containerd 2.4.0)

`ctr` attempts to parse `-uexc` as a flag for `ctr run` itself and aborts:

```
Incorrect Usage: flag provided but not defined: -uexc

ctr: flag provided but not defined: -uexc
```

### Additional Context & Impact

* **Regression source:** This behavior changed with the CLI migration from `urfave/cli/v2` to `urfave/cli/v3` in 2.4.0. In `v2`, Go's standard library `flag.FlagSet` stopped flag parsing at the first positional argument (`Image`), leaving all subsequent arguments untouched in `c.Args().Slice()[2:]`. In `v3`, the argument scanner continues looking for flags throughout the remaining arguments.
* **Compatibility impact with `--`:** Existing scripts and automation cannot simply insert `--` after the container ID (`ctr run <image> <id> -- <cmd>`) to support both old and new versions. In `containerd <= 2.3.x`, `ctr` does not strip `--` when placed after positional arguments; it passes `"--"` directly to runc as the process command, failing with:
  ```
  exec: "--": executable file not found in $PATH
  ```
* This also affects other commands taking positional container commands, such as `ctr exec`.
14208.author: chenglongtang1
